stemMd: An ideal gas is heated in a rigid sealed container. What boundary work does it do as its temperature rises?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The same as all heat absorbed

options.label: D
options.textMd: A positive amount because temperature rises

explanationMd: Boundary work is the integral of pressure with respect to volume. A rigid container has no volume change, so this work is zero even though pressure and internal energy can rise.

distractorRationale.b: Finite heating does not imply infinite work.
distractorRationale.d: Pressure can rise without boundary displacement.
distractorRationale.e: No volume change means no compression work either.
distractorRationale.a: That would require a different energy balance.
